title: Health Assessment of Higher Education System in Three-dimensions

limitations: GDM sum (4), entropy formulas (5)-(7), and the Verhulst block (15)-(18) are OCR-scrambled.
Index table effect column is misaligned with the prose. Prose is treated as authoritative.
Sensitivity tables print beta1 = 0.16 and beta2 = 0.26 against 0.0016 and 0.0026 in the equations.
Running headers in a decorative font leak into the text layer on every page.

tasks: Build an evaluation model for the health of a national higher education system
Apply it to several countries and pick one with room to improve
Set an achievable target using non-educational constraints
Give targeted policies with a timeline
Test the policies and discuss how hard change is

section_map.summary: Three dimensions, modulus and angle, India chosen, curved target, Verhulst check.
Burke quotation, two-part definition, task list ending in the difficulty of change.
Nationality rule, equal experts, no mutation, accurate official data.
22 countries, three fill rules, three index types, blended weights, eight countries scored.
HDI, FSI, Gini set a cap of radius 1.22 inside an 11.5 degree cone for India.
Angle first, modulus later. Three terms, each step named with a number.
No-policy decline against policy path. Five groups, each with a benefit and a cost.
One coefficient group moved at a time. Three strengths, two weaknesses.

contributions.summary: Health is the modulus and sustainability is the angle to (1,1,1), so the two are not one number.
The target is a spherical cap, not a point, because balance is a range.
Every affected group gets a benefit paragraph and a cost paragraph marked with a triangle.

dependency_graph.handoff: Current modulus, current angle, and the three components fix the starting point of the target cap
The three component series are what the grey model forecasts, with and without policy
The 11.5 degree cone is the bar the 2040 policy forecast is judged against

assumptions.summary: Nationality fixes which system a student belongs to.
Experts are equally skilled and the questions have no real ambiguity.
The system is continuous, slow, and self-healing, so it does not jump.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 22 countries, 20 data sets, 12 indices. Gaps filled by neighbor mean, by a similar series, or by a fitted curve.

models.summary: 3DVA: blended weights, vector modulus for health, angle for balance.
CST: HDI, FSI, and Gini push a cap of radius 1.22 inside an 11.5 degree cone.
N-Verhulst: grey forecast of the three components with and without policy.

verification.summary: Eight countries. UK most balanced, US strongest, India weak on both.
Policy turns student treatment from a 3.2 percent yearly fall to a 0.6 percent rise.
Small coefficient changes move the cap only slightly.

results_trace.summary: Blend 0.85 expert, 0.15 entropy. ECS near half of social influence. Education cost only 9 percent of student treatment.
UK 0.881 at 1.15 degrees. US 1.278 at 11.90. India 0.735 at 23.13. China 0.955 at 24.52. South Africa 0.660 at 30.65.
India target radius 1.22, cone 11.5 degrees. Component gains 41.3, 20.4, 306 percent.
2040 policy vector (0.58, 0.61, 0.50), angle under 11.5 degrees. Summary sheet: 0.978 and 4.86 against 0.640 and 29.96 with no policy.

writing_logic.summary: Summary runs Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly, In the end. Each block is one model.
Each index gets a name, a reason, a data source, and a target value. The repeated shape is the argument.
Impact section is five pairs. Benefit first, then a triangle and the cost. The closing paragraph says why the costs win in the short run.

language_observations.summary: Burke quoted in four words of setup, then a belief sentence. The quotation is not explained.
The definition has two halves, developed and balanced, and the model later computes exactly those two halves.
'It is its objectivity that is the reason' — one property, one method.
Cannikin's law named once, as the warrant that one strong component cannot save a weak one.
'By the way' introduces the pre-emption of GDP per capita, which is already inside HDI and FSI.
They concede the path bends: pushing one part disturbs the others, so the track is a curve.
'The resistance is always in front of us' against benefits that take a long span. Time asymmetry, not a number, closes the section.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1: flow diagram of the whole solution.
Figure 2: integrated weights for the three dimensions.
Figure 3: schematic of S, S0, and the differential vector.
Figures 4 and 5: eight country vectors in two panels.
Figure 6: India's target cap with the current vector and the edge point.
Figure 7: trend chart, angle falling first, modulus rising later.
Figure 8: implementation timeline for the three terms.
Figure 9: no-policy and policy paths over 20 years.
Figures 10 and 11: caps under the two perturbed coefficient groups.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A named folk law, the bucket, does the work of a proof: the angle punishes the short stave.
The order of policies is read off the figure, angle first and level second, so the timeline is not a preference.
The paper argues against its own policies at length. That costs space and buys credibility.

weaknesses.summary: Authors: little is said about how education change hits other industries.
Authors: long decimals were rounded and may move the result.
Elasticity coefficients are stipulated, and the sensitivity table contradicts the equations.

independent_extensions.summary: Fit the six coefficients to a panel instead of stating them.
Publish the series length, the parameters, and one hold-out error.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: A system scored on level and on balance at once, with balance read as an angle to an equal vector.
Policies ordered by the diagnosed gap, short term on the weakest part, and each step given a number.

unresolved_questions.question: Which beta values were actually used, the equation scale or the table scale?
Does the policy path come from the Verhulst equation, or is it drawn by hand?
